## Observation
In Windows sweep run 44456347985 (job 135332660982, main at ab323f7df0c), `tests/unit/reconciler/apply/test_bridge_state_atomic_write_concurrency.py::test_peer_confirmations_distinct_concurrent_saves_are_merged` failed with `PermissionError(13, 'Permission denied')` recorded by the test's concurrent READER thread (`final_path.read_text()`, `:43-47`), not by the writers. The writers now retry a contended replace (`rebar._store.fsutil.replace_with_retry`, sporting-feudalist-bluet). On Windows, opening a file while `MoveFileEx(MOVEFILE_REPLACE_EXISTING)` replaces it can fail with access denied; POSIX readers never see this.

## Hypotheses (unproven)
- Product readers that open a published sidecar, cache or cursor without holding the writer's lock (for example a store's initial load) can get the same transient `PermissionError` on Windows and treat it as a failed or empty read.
- Readers that already read under the sibling lock (`sidecar_transactions.mutate_json_object`) are unaffected.

## Enumeration
The full enumeration (not exposed, lock-protected, exposed-but-harmless cache misses) is recorded in this ticket's comment of 2026-11-19. No read-side retry exists in the tree; the only `PermissionError` handling around a publish is the writer's `replace_with_retry` (`src/rebar/_store/fsutil.py:45-65`).

Exposed with a harmful outcome (crash, a silent wrong default, or a lost write), all fixed here:
- Crash / fail-closed: `_store/compat.py:341` (`_analyze`, reached from `lock.acquire` at `_store/lock.py:373`, so every write command fails while an ensure republishes the record) and `:164` (`_local_store_epoch`); `_config_sources.py:120,128` (`rebar.toml` stat and open; also reached by `_config_writer.py:221`); `_cli/__init__.py:174`; `llm/evals/eval.py:80`; `llm/evals/provider_parity.py:221`; `reconciler/projects_store.py:69`; `reconciler/binding_repository.py:262`; `_engine_support/bridge_fsck.py:68-71`; `llm/workflow/completion_banking.py:543`.
- Lost or wrong write: `_commands/session_log.py:55` (an unreadable pointer starts a new session log and overwrites the pointer); `_commands/bridge_repair.py:68` (an empty retired set disables Guard 2 before `save()`); `_snapshot/cache.py:92` (`byte_total` read as 0 makes `janitor.py:314-315` add the full total again); `reconciler/get_rotation.py:30`; `llm/gate_runs.py:179` (a terminal record read as absent can be overwritten by `_materialize_stale_running`, `:389-403`).
- Silent wrong default: `llm/prompting/prompts.py:190,351,522` (a user prompt override silently replaced by the packaged prompt); `_commands/identity.py:38` (events stamped without the current identity); `_store/push_state.py:143` (PUSH_PENDING hidden); `_store/ensures.py:113,207`; `_commands/scratch.py:158`; `_ids.py:119`; `_engine_support/bridge_fsck_drift.py:21`; `reconciler/alert_store.py:63,123`; `reconciler/last_pass.py:183`; `reconciler/binding_repository.py:196,284`; `reconciler/peer_confirmations.py:71`; `reconciler/impossible_links.py:195`; `llm/plan_review/checkpoints.py:117` and `llm/workflow/completion_verdict_cache.py:258` (a refused read reruns a billable LLM call).

## Approach
Move the contended-path retry loop out of `replace_with_retry` into one helper, `fsutil.retry_contended(fn, *args, **kwargs)`: on Windows it retries `PermissionError` with the existing backoff and 2 s deadline (`_REPLACE_RETRY_DEADLINE_S`), then re-raises; elsewhere it calls `fn` once. `replace_with_retry` becomes `retry_contended(os.replace, src, dst)`, unchanged in behaviour. Add `fsutil.open_published(path, mode="r", *, encoding="utf-8")`, which is `retry_contended(open, ...)` (encoding omitted for binary modes); the refusal happens when the file is opened, so retrying the open is enough. Each exposed reader above replaces its `open(...)`/`Path.read_text(...)` with `open_published(...)` (and `_config_sources.py:120` wraps its `path.stat()` in `retry_contended`), keeping its existing exception handling, so a refusal that outlasts the deadline still takes the same path as today. A refused replace also refuses a stat, so an existence check before the open is exposed in the same way: `Path.exists()`/`is_file()` re-raise `PermissionError` on Python 3.11/3.12 and return False on 3.13+, and `os.path.exists`/`isfile` return False. Where a listed reader checks existence of the file it then opens (`binding_repository.py:193,260,281`, `projects_store.py:66`, `prompts.py:189,350`, `scratch.py:154`, `checkpoints.py:116`, `eval.py:77`, `bridge_repair.py:65`, and any other such check in a listed reader), the check is removed and `FileNotFoundError` raised by `open_published` maps to the reader's existing absent branch. Absence is then decided only by an open, and only `PermissionError` is retried. Existence checks that gate a read but sit outside a reader function use a third helper, `fsutil.published_is_file(path)`: `stat.S_ISREG(retry_contended(os.stat, path).st_mode)`, mapping `FileNotFoundError`/`NotADirectoryError` to False. It replaces `is_file()` on published config files in `_config_sources._discover_project_config` (`rt.is_file()` `:175` for `rebar.toml`, `pp.is_file()` `:184` for `pyproject.toml`) and `raw_layers` (`up.is_file()` `:209`, the user config), and `os.path.exists` on `.store-compat.json` in `_store/store_usability._carries_store_structure` (`:55`). Without it, a refused stat on Python 3.13+ makes discovery silently skip the project `rebar.toml` while `_config_writer.py:221` republishes it. POSIX behaviour is unchanged: on POSIX both helpers are a single direct call. Reusing the existing Windows switch `_RETRY_CONTENDED_REPLACE` adds no config key, environment variable or flag.

The unlocked read-modify-write in `alert_store.patch_bug_filed` (`alert_store.py:118-147`) can also drop an append made between its read and its replace, on every platform. That is a separate race, not this Windows read refusal; it is filed as equable-overseas-hoiho.

## Scope
- `src/rebar/_store/fsutil.py` (`retry_contended`, `open_published`, `published_is_file`; `replace_with_retry` delegates)
- `src/rebar/_store/store_usability.py` (`_carries_store_structure`)
- The reader modules listed under "Exposed with a harmful outcome" (one call-site swap each)
- `tests/unit/store/test_fsutil_read_retry.py` (new)

## Testing
- New unit tests force the Windows branch (`monkeypatch.setattr(fsutil, "_RETRY_CONTENDED_REPLACE", True)`) and inject an `open` that raises `PermissionError` twice and then succeeds: `open_published` returns the content; a refusal that outlasts a shortened deadline re-raises `PermissionError`; `FileNotFoundError` propagates at once. On the POSIX branch one `PermissionError` propagates immediately.
- A wiring test parses each fixed reader module and asserts each listed reader function (including `_discover_project_config`, `raw_layers` and `_carries_store_structure`) calls `open_published`, `retry_contended` or `published_is_file` and makes no `exists()`/`is_file()`/`os.path.exists`/`os.path.isfile` call, so the enumeration cannot silently regress.
- For each reader whose existence guard is removed, its existing absent-file test (or a new one in the new test module) still gets the absent default when the file does not exist.
- Existing `replace_with_retry` tests keep passing; `make verify` passes.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] The product read paths of files published through `atomic_write`/`replace_with_retry` are enumerated, and each is recorded as either lock-protected or exposed on Windows.
- [x] Every exposed read path tolerates the transient refusal (or is shown not to need to), with a Windows-branch unit test.
